name: How do you compare bids for a multi-family project?

mainEntity.name: What is the best way to compare contractor or project management proposals for apartment and condo work?
mainEntity.text: What is the best way to compare contractor or project management proposals for apartment and condo work?

acceptedAnswer.text: Multi-family bids should be compared on more than price alone. The most useful comparison looks at scope completeness, exclusions, allowances, schedule assumptions, staffing, quality expectations, and how change orders are handled. Two proposals can have similar totals but very different risk profiles if one includes more detail, stronger supervision, or better coordination. Owners should ask whether resident communication, site protection, permits, inspections, and closeout are included. If the project is occupied or phased, that should be clearly reflected in the proposal. A bid that seems cheaper may leave out critical coordination work and cost more later through delays or extras. The best approach is to compare proposals line by line and confirm exactly what each firm is responsible for before making a decision.
acceptedAnswer.description: Compare bids by scope, exclusions, schedule assumptions, allowances, supervision, and change-order terms rather than just the total price. The lowest number is not always the best value if key items are missing or the proposal assumes unrealistic conditions.
